findings.title: 0310 recuts a body with an existing, documented pin and never re-measures it -- packages/db/tests/knowledge-retrieval.test.mjs's p658.census.no_recut is left red
findings.standard_cited: packages/db/README.md:193-241 (the pin-recut convention): a later migration whose own number is below the pinning migration's, and which recuts the pinned function, must locate every existing pin on that function and re-measure each one against the function's NEW body, in the SAME COMMIT as the recut -- the pin does not update itself. 0310 (#1031) is numbered below the pinning test file's own governing migration 0230, so this is squarely the rule's own case, not the 'recut is numbered above the pin' exception on the same page.
findings.evidence: migrations/0310_knowledge_fye_pair_wall.sql recuts clara._knowledge_capture_core (the migration's own header names it as one of the two bodies recut). tests/knowledge-retrieval.test.mjs lines 938-970 (cell p658.census.no_recut) already pins that exact signature's sha256(prosrc) at 2c8526b82d54ac0aa49c77c3be277be5ecd9cad73df0fec63908d67a0681b01b (the pre-0310 body -- the same value 0310's own prestate measured), and is documented in tests/README.md:990 as one of the file's own house census cells. The SAME cell already demonstrates the fix this convention requires: its own comment (lines 939-946) narrates how #885 (migration 0268) recut clara.answer_work_question, one of this cell's other seven pins, and how that recutting ticket came back into this file and updated the pin with a migration-liveness-conditional branch. #1031 did not repeat that pattern for its own recut of _knowledge_capture_core. Reproduced live: node --test --test-concurrency=1 $GATES tests/knowledge-retrieval.test.mjs against 127.0.0.1:55746/clara_l06 -- 27 pass, 1 fail: p658.census.no_recut fails with 'clara._knowledge_capture_core(...) is NOT at its measured pre-0230 body', measured sha 98bcbe3589c1813da4bbdb7f5486db0d4996e831050a86cd810e25d28554ce06 vs the file's own pinned 2c8526b8.... A direct pg query against the same catalogue independently confirms the live body now hashes to 98bcbe35..., matching the failure exactly. Ticket #1031's own report (wave4-lane06-ticket1031.md) names knowledge-fye-day.test.mjs, knowledge-firm-defaults.test.mjs and knowledge-onboarding-promotion.test.mjs as the files it ran -- knowledge-retrieval.test.mjs, which pins the very body 0310 recuts, is not in that list and was not run. Ticket #1038's report later found this failure as a bystander (running the full package suite as unrequired bonus diligence) and correctly declined to fix it as out of its own scope (work order rule 5), but it is #1031's own migration that caused it and #1031's own commit that owed the re-measurement under the cited convention.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone who runs packages/db's test suite (or the full gate chain, or an integrator's from-scratch proof) on top of this lane's branch sees tests/knowledge-retrieval.test.mjs fail at p658.census.no_recut, with no accompanying fix or explanation in that file, contradicting the file's own established convention for exactly this situation and leaving a false 'this body is unmoved since before 0230' claim on the record.
findings.required_fix: In #1031's own commit (or a follow-up on this same lane before integration), update tests/knowledge-retrieval.test.mjs's p658.census.no_recut pin for clara._knowledge_capture_core the same way #885 updated the answer_work_question pin: either replace the literal with the new post-0310 body's sha (98bcbe35...), or -- if 0310's presence should itself be optional/conditional on this rig the way work_source_correction_supersede is -- branch the pin on whether 0310 is applied, mirroring the existing sourceCorrectionLive pattern in the same cell.

findings.title: 0311 changes TIN's seeding behaviour (undetermined-and-held-back -> always-seeded-optional) without updating firm-setup-polish.test.mjs's hardcoded seed count, leaving it red
findings.standard_cited: No single line is violated as cleanly as std-1's, but this is the same class of defect the README's consumer/pin discipline (packages/db/README.md:193-241) exists to prevent -- a migration that changes a body's observable behaviour is responsible for re-deriving every existing assertion that depended on the old behaviour, in the same commit -- and it directly falsifies ticket #1038's own Agent Brief acceptance criterion, 'The whole database suite passes with the fixtures moved (every battery that mints a client).' #1038 did not cause this regression, but that AC is not currently true on this branch.
findings.evidence: migrations/0311_firm_setup_tin_required.sql makes tin read required or optional for every firm (never undetermined/held-back) per the owner's Option A ruling. Reproduced live: node --test --test-concurrency=1 $GATES tests/firm-setup-polish.test.mjs against 127.0.0.1:55746/clara_l06 -- 2 pass, 1 fail: p895.seed.noop (tests/firm-setup-polish.test.mjs:66) asserts a first reconciliation seed inserts exactly 13 items and gets 14 ('AssertionError: 14 !== 13'), because tin is now seeded on the very first reconciliation where it used to be held back as undetermined. Ticket #1032's own report (wave4-lane06-ticket1032.md) lists its own gate files as firm-setup-applicability.test.mjs, firm-setup.test.mjs, firm-setup-user-notes.test.mjs and firm-setup-education-tips.test.mjs -- firm-setup-polish.test.mjs, which independently counts seeded items off the same catalogue #1032's migration re-seeds, is not among them and was not run by #1032's own implementer. Ticket #1038's report (wave4-lane06-ticket1038.md, 'What I found and fixed', item 4) found and correctly attributed this same failure as a bystander during an unrequired full-suite run, and declined to fix it as out of #1038's own scope -- correctly, since #1038 did not cause it, but it is left unrepaired on the lane's HEAD as things stand.
findings.failure_scenario: The same full-suite or from-scratch proof that trips std-1 also trips firm-setup-polish.test.mjs's p895.seed.noop, and an integrator or a later lane reconciling firm-setup seeding counts elsewhere in the suite has no signal that #1032 is the cause unless they read #1038's report by chance.
findings.required_fix: Update tests/firm-setup-polish.test.mjs's p895.seed.noop literal (13 -> 14, and re-check any other literal in that file keyed off the pre-#1032 seeded-item count) in the same lane, ideally folded back into #1032's own commit per the work order's migration-house-law spirit, before this lane integrates.

clean_by_verification: Ticket order in the lane branch (#1031, #1032, #1038) matches the WAVE-4 LANE RULES.

#1032 implements Option A exactly as the owner's 2026-09-23 ruling comment on gh issue #1032 states (TIN always seeded, required only when turnover makes MyInvois mandatory, optional otherwise with an answer form in both cases, required_outstanding/commit door count it only when required, mpers_eligibility unchanged).

#1038's migration number is 0316 as reserved; #1031's is 0310; #1032's is 0311 -- all free, none reused, no applied migration edited (git diff cd2925391...HEAD --stat shows exactly these three new migration files and no other migration touched).
None of the three migrations create a new relation, so the FORCE RLS / zero-application-role-DML rule does not apply to any of them.
None of the three migrations touch the standard-chart rows migration 0295 references or inserts into it; rule (d) does not apply to this lane.

Prestate pins in all three migrations were independently re-measured against the live clara_l06 catalogue via a direct pg connection and matched exactly: clara._knowledge_assert_value (84fca940...), clara.set_client_fy_end (d8aaadbb...), clara.create_client body (7e8ff7f2...) all confirmed byte-identical to their pinned pre-images; clara.create_client's clara_authenticated EXECUTE grant confirmed withdrawn (false).

Owner/SECURITY DEFINER/search_path/ACL preservation on every recut body was checked in each migration's own tail and spot-verified structurally; no grant widened to PUBLIC or to an application role beyond what each migration's own argument requires.

The gate-chain entries for fye-pair-wall, firm-setup-tin-required and create-client-grant-withdrawn preintegration gates were appended to packages/db/package.json's test script in migration-number order (0310, 0311, 0316) after the existing chain, with no reordering of earlier entries.
No applied migration was edited; no frozen workflow or manifest was touched (packages/runtime untouched by all three tickets); no docs/PRD.md or docs/ARCHITECTURE.md edit.

Directly re-ran and confirmed exact reported pass/fail counts for: tests/knowledge-fye-day.test.mjs (10/10), tests/firm-setup-applicability.test.mjs (5/5), tests/client-birth-wall.test.mjs (15/15), tests/operation-census.test.mjs (10/10), tests/rig-isolation.test.mjs (22 pass/1 skip) -- every one of these matches the per-ticket reports' own claimed numbers exactly.

CONTEXT.md's 'Firm setup applicability' entry was rewritten in place (not appended) per house convention, correctly distinguishing the two now-live shapes (asked-or-not for mpers_eligibility, required-or-optional for tin) with its own Avoid line.

The migration-and-battery-as-one-unit shape with a vacuity control (deliberately breaking the new rule, observing the predicted red, restoring byte-for-byte) is used consistently across all three tickets in place of a literal pre-authoring red-before-green cycle, which the work order's own wave-3 addendum and this repo's established convention for migration-shaped tickets sanction; no horizontal-slicing anti-pattern (a whole battery of red tests committed before any implementation) was found in any of the six commits' diffs.

No Fowler smell baseline judgement call rose above routine: the ~12-file caller migration in #1038 (Shotgun Surgery in shape) is the ticket's own stated deliverable, not an avoidable side effect, and each call site's edit is a minimal, mechanical swap onto the same new helper rather than divergent bespoke logic.
